paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD of Hosts speaks over Damascus, over Kedar and Hazor, and over Elam, and none of them gets to run the show. Damascus panics, the nation at ease with no gates or bars sits there feeling safe, and Elam leans on its bow (Jeremiah 49:24, 31, 35). Strength, walls and a quiet life are all nice, but none of them is the one holding the world together.

Now watch what the LORD says in the middle of the hard word. He calls Damascus "the city of praise" and "the town that brings Me joy" (Jeremiah 49:25). Then at the very end of the Elam message He says, "Yet in the last days, I will restore Elam from captivity," (Jeremiah 49:39). I think that tells us something big, friend: the LORD is the one who decides how each word ends, and for Elam He ends it with restoring.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Don't put your whole weight on a bow, a wall or a lucky streak, because the LORD can shatter any of them. Put your weight on the LORD, who sees every nation and has the last word over each one. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, it is good to belong to the One who has the last word.
